  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a Python CLI that reads sales CSV files and prints total revenue, revenue per region, and units per product; the result is usable from the repository checkout and visible on standard output when invoked. S2 — Fact: deliver tests for the requested behavior. Boundary: this is intake only, the repository is empty, and no implementation is made in this stage. Assumption: the checkout is the delivery target; no deployment is authorized or required by the request. An isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; any deployed outcome would be visible only after release. Discovery leads: inspect the available runtime and any authorized sample sales data or schema; no team, channel, internal site, document, private repository, owner, or sensitive locator is named. Treat leads as unverified and keep any sensitive locator in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/. Open questions are assigned to discovery or recorded defaults in Q1–Q11, with their prerequisites and blockers stated there. The product is a noninteractive CLI: the invoking user supplies file paths, the operating system identifies that user, and no application-level actor identification or shared session state is assumed; the recorded state default rules out collaboration and persistence, while filesystem and terminal access remain governed by the runtime environment."
